summary.text: MaryJane Shimsky is a Democratic member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 92 in Westchester County since January 2023 and is running for re-election on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines.
She previously served on the Westchester County Board of Legislators from 2011 to 2022.

paragraphs.text: MaryJane Shimsky is a native of Scranton, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Yale University and New York University School of Law; she also earned a PhD in history from the City University of New York.
She and her husband have lived in the Rivertowns area of Westchester County for 30 years, and their two children attended public schools in Hastings-on-Hudson.

From 2011 to 2022 Shimsky served on the Westchester County Board of Legislators, where, according to her official biography, she worked on the environment, flood mitigation, infrastructure and public health.
She sponsored the county legislation to protect access to women's health clinics and to raise the tobacco age to 21.
Shimsky's Assembly district includes most of the towns of Greenburgh and Mount Pleasant and part of northwest Yonkers.

She serves on the Assembly committees on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Governmental Operations; Judiciary; Local Governments; Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development; and Transportation.
Her biography lists enacted legislation on food donation and food scraps recycling, e-filing in lower courts and school tax payment schedules, among other measures.
